solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Intentionally signed off after purchase delivered (2,6)

indicatorNotes.off: off = gone wrong, so the letters of SIGNED are rearranged
indicatorNotes.delivered: a speech is delivered, so this word is spoken, not spelt
indicatorNotes.after: the anagram comes after the sound-alike

blocks.note: to buy = to purchase; said out loud it is BY
SIGNED rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone deliberately signs off a delivery once the purchase has arrived.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Signed off' reads as one phrase about approving a delivery; the setter splits it into fodder and indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something by design means doing it on purpose, intentionally.

entries.clue: Repercussion that’s best dealt with by another near Bath? (8)

annotation.definition2: that’s best dealt with by another near Bath?

blocks.note: an unwelcome after-effect, like the wash a boat leaves behind

blocks.clueFragment: that’s best dealt with by another near Bath?
blocks.note: read literally: the part of you someone else scrubs best, in the tub

annotation.surface: A playful question about some consequence that needs a helper, somewhere near the city of Bath.
annotation.walkthrough: Bath is capitalised to pass as the English city; really it is the tub, and the helper scrubs your back. The question mark flags the whimsy.
annotation.definitionFit: Backwash is the wake a boat leaves, and so figuratively the repercussions of an event.

entries.clue: Senior copper bags stolen garment (5)

indicatorNotes.bags: to bag is to hold inside, so DI holds HOT

blocks.note: DI = Detective Inspector, a senior police officer
hot = stolen, as in hot goods

annotation.surface: A senior police officer confiscates a stolen item of clothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is British slang for a police officer; a DI is a Detective Inspector.
annotation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the loincloth garment worn by men in India.

entries.clue: Economic relationship with flexibility, as a consequence exact (6,3,6)

blocks.note: supply is the adverb of supple: in a flexible way
and = with the result that, as in 'push and it opens'
to exact payment is to demand it

annotation.surface: A dry line from an economics text about flexible relationships and exact consequences.
annotation.walkthrough: SUPPLY here is not the noun but the rare adverb from supple, pronounced SUP-lee; the surface hides that under the economics.
annotation.definitionFit: Supply and demand is the basic economic relationship that sets prices.

entries.clue: Break down dispute cycling medal introduces (2,5)

indicatorNotes.cycling: cycling moves the first letter of ROW to the back
indicatorNotes.introduces: the medal takes the cycled word inside it

blocks.note: a gong is British slang for a medal or award
row = dispute, with R cycled to the end

annotation.surface: A quarrel about cycling that ends with a medal being introduced.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'cycling' a sport alongside the medal; it is the instruction to rotate ROW.
annotation.definitionFit: A machine that breaks down has gone wrong.

entries.clue: Gruesome ban following change of leadership (6)

indicatorNotes.following change of leadership: the first letter, the leader, is changed

blocks.note: forbid = ban
F swapped for M

annotation.surface: A grisly ban imposed after a new leader takes over.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter does not say which new letter comes in; only M makes a word meaning gruesome.
annotation.definitionFit: Morbid means taking an unhealthy interest in death and gruesome things.

entries.clue: Where marine life will never be happy (2,3,2,3,5)

annotation.definition: Where marine life will never be

blocks.clueFragment: Where marine life will never be
blocks.note: literally, up on a mountain summit, far from the sea
elated, as if standing on a summit

annotation.surface: A gloomy thought that sea creatures are doomed never to be happy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two halves together as one sentence about unhappy fish; split after 'be', and the first half is a place, taken literally.
annotation.definitionFit: Feeling on top of the world means feeling very happy.

entries.clue: Biblical adulterer, extremely tough female, crushed by degrees (9)

indicatorNotes.extremely: only the extremes, the first and last letters, of tough
indicatorNotes.crushed by: TH and SHE are squeezed between the two degrees

blocks.note: BA = Bachelor of Arts, a degree
outer letters of ToUgH
she = a female
the second degree, another BA

annotation.surface: A tough woman from the Bible being crushed little by little.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By degrees' reads as gradually; here the degrees are two BAs, and the plural tells you to use two.
annotation.definitionFit: Bathsheba committed adultery with King David in the Old Testament.

entries.clue: A little lower on the right-hand side (6)

blocks.note: a lower is one that lows, a cow; here a small Irish breed of cattle
the heraldic Latin term for right

annotation.surface: A direction to set something slightly lower on the right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as 'more low'; it is really one that lows, a cow, and the Dexter is a small Irish breed.
annotation.definitionFit: Dexter is Latin for right, used for the right-hand side of a shield.

entries.clue: On policing, essentially Eastern girl bites tongue (6)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence, the middle, of policing
indicatorNotes.bites: GAL has E between its teeth
indicatorNotes.On: in a down clue, IC sits on top of GAEL, i.e. after it

blocks.note: gal = girl
E = East
the two middle letters of polICing

annotation.surface: A girl from the East, on police duty, holds her tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bites tongue' suggests keeping quiet; 'tongue' is the definition, a language.
annotation.definitionFit: Gaelic is the Celtic language of Ireland and Scotland.

entries.clue: Chew some pork that’s medium on the inside (5)

indicatorNotes.on the inside: whatever is on the inside sits within its host, so medium sits within the pork cut

blocks.note: a pork chop
M = medium, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: Eating a pork chop cooked medium in the middle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Medium on the inside' reads like a cooking instruction, and the answer is what you do next.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe working food between the teeth, the answer adding noise and vigour.

entries.clue: One upshot of having much demand on the law changed (6,3)

indicatorNotes.changed: a law that is changed no longer reads as before, so its letters take a new order
indicatorNotes.on: TAX is placed after, on the end of, the anagram

blocks.note: THE LAW rearranged
a tax is a demand for money

annotation.surface: A complaint that a change in the law has made great demands of people.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram comes last in the clue but first in the answer; 'on' puts TAX after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A wealth tax is a levy on the rich, a consequence of having a lot.

entries.clue: Eddy’s hands wrapped in trendy fleece gloves (9)

indicatorNotes.wrapped in: something wrapped in a covering sits inside it, so the hands sit inside trendy
indicatorNotes.gloves: WOOL covers HIRLP as a glove covers a hand

blocks.note: a sheep's fleece is its wool
hip = trendy
right and left hands

annotation.surface: A man called Eddy wears trendy fleece gloves.
annotation.walkthrough: Eddy looks like a man's name owning the hands; it is the definition, a swirl of water, with 's standing for 'is'. Two containers nest, and the inner one is built first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an eddy is water swirling round in a circle, the same thing as the answer on a smaller scale.

entries.clue: Attitude entertains small group of friends (5)

indicatorNotes.entertains: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so POSE holds S

blocks.note: a pose = an attitude, a posture
S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A certain attitude plays host to a small circle of friends.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition uses posse in its slang sense of a gang of mates, not a sheriff's band.
annotation.definitionFit: Posse is slang for someone's crew or group of friends.

entries.clue: Setter is taken in by semi-optimistic primate (7)

indicatorNotes.is taken in by: to be taken in is to be admitted inside, so the setter's words go inside the half-word
indicatorNotes.semi-: semi = half, so only the first half of sanguine

blocks.note: half of SANGuine, optimistic
the setter refers to themself: I AM

annotation.surface: A crossword setter admits being fooled by a primate that is only half hopeful.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter is 'I' in crosswords, so 'setter is' becomes I AM. A siamang is not a common word; the wordplay builds it.
annotation.definitionFit: The siamang is a large black gibbon of Southeast Asia, a primate.

entries.clue: Dodging deacon via dithering (9)

indicatorNotes.dithering: letters that dither wobble out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A dithering church deacon takes an evasive route.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Via' is part of the fodder, not a link word.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun-for-noun match: 'dodging' here names the act, as a gerund, just as the answer does.

entries.clue: Before payment, barely eat and drink (6)

indicatorNotes.barely: bare means stripped, so scoff loses its outer letters
indicatorNotes.Before: before means in front of, so the eating part is placed in front of the payment

blocks.note: SCOFF = eat, stripped of its outer letters
a fee is a payment

annotation.surface: Someone eats and drinks sparingly before paying the bill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Barely' reads as 'hardly'; it means undressed, taking the outside letters off SCOFF.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by the wider class: the answer is one particular drink, the kind usually ordered at a café before paying.

entries.clue: Go before stake and surrender (8)

blocks.note: the ante is the stake put up in poker
to cede = to surrender

annotation.surface: A gambler bets first and then gives in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go before stake' looks like instructions to a card player; 'Go before' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym built from Latin: ante means before and cedere to go.

entries.clue: Very valuable ancient information banks (6)

indicatorNotes.banks: GEN banks OLD on both sides, like river banks

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
old = ancient

annotation.surface: Old databanks of information prove highly valuable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Information banks' reads as databanks; banks is the verb here, meaning flanks.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: gold is precious, so anything given its adjective is treated as highly valuable, as with an opportunity.

entries.clue: 10? — the ultimate position for Gordon Brown (6)

indicatorNotes.the ultimate position for: the letter in the last position of Gordon

blocks.note: last letter of GordoN
umber = a brown pigment

annotation.surface: Number 10 Downing Street, the last post Gordon Brown held.
annotation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was Prime Minister, living at Number 10 Downing Street, so the surface points at the answer twice. The question mark marks 10 as one example of a number; it is not the cross-reference it looks like.
annotation.definitionFit: Ten is a number, hence the question mark for definition by example.

entries.clue: Arab revolutionary patrolling hospital in sheikhdom (7)

indicatorNotes.revolutionary: ARAB is overturned, its letters rearranged
indicatorNotes.patrolling: a patrol goes round, so BARA surrounds H

blocks.note: ARAB rearranged
H = hospital, as on road signs
the word itself

annotation.surface: An Arab rebel guards a hospital in a Gulf kingdom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word joining the wordplay to the definition, but it supplies the last two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Bahrain is a Gulf state ruled by a sheikh, so a sheikhdom.

entries.clue: Drag queen, formerly from lingerie club (7)

indicatorNotes.Drag: to drag something out is to pull it away
indicatorNotes.from: ER is taken out from the lingerie word

blocks.note: a brassiere is lingerie
ER = Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

annotation.surface: A drag queen who used to perform at a lingerie nightclub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drag queen' is the obvious phrase, but 'Drag' is the removal instruction. 'Formerly' is there because Elizabeth II has died, so ER is now a former queen.
annotation.definitionFit: A brassie is an old name for a golf club, the two-wood.

entries.clue: Show off on board, appealing fare? (3,3)

blocks.note: to perform flashy tricks on a surfboard or skateboard
food from a stand; appealing because a roll wraps the sausage, like peel

annotation.surface: Showing off on a ship, with tempting food on offer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; it is a surfboard. The question mark admits 'appealing' is a pun: the sausage comes in a roll, a kind of peel.
annotation.definitionFit: To hot-dog is to show off with tricks, especially surfing.

entries.clue: Man giving up coat for senior citizen (5)

indicatorNotes.giving up coat: the outer layer of letters is shed

blocks.note: a man = a soldier, as in officers and men
S and R, the outer letters, removed

annotation.surface: A man hands over his coat to an elderly person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a soldier: the ranks are 'the men'. The coat is the outside pair of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An oldie is an informal word for an old person.

entries.clue: When email fails in the interim (9)

indicatorNotes.fails: the letters collapse into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: What to do while the email is down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'When' looks like it starts a sentence; it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for an adverb: both mean during the time between two events.

entries.clue: Animal caught in spin-drier (5)

indicatorNotes.caught in: the answer is trapped inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the hyphen, between sp and er

annotation.surface: A pet trapped in the tumble drier.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen hides the join: the letters run across it.
annotation.definitionFit: The indri is a large lemur of Madagascar.

entries.clue: Converting garden, use work clothes (9)

indicatorNotes.Converting: the letters are converted into a new word

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Advice to wear overalls when converting a garden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Use' reads as the verb of the instruction but belongs to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Dungarees are overalls, the work clothes of gardeners and mechanics.

entries.clue: Porter maybe abandoning poet in mountainous region (5)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: COLE is left behind when leaving the poet's name

blocks.note: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
Cole Porter, the songwriter; 'maybe' flags an example

annotation.surface: A porter quits the job and leaves a poet stranded in the mountains.
annotation.walkthrough: Porter seems to be a luggage carrier; it is a surname, and the first name Cole is what goes.
annotation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long stretch of high mountain ground.

entries.clue: Grasping cap on gas piping (6)

indicatorNotes.cap on: the cap of a word is its first letter, placed on top

blocks.note: first letter of Gas
a piping voice is thin and reedy

annotation.surface: A plumber reaching for the cap on a gas pipe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piping' suggests pipes for gas; it is the high thin sound of a reed pipe.
annotation.definitionFit: Grasping means greedy for money or possessions.

entries.clue: Prompt cat eats last of mice and departs (4-4)

indicatorNotes.last of: only the final letter of mice
indicatorNotes.eats: FELINE takes E and D inside

blocks.note: a feline = a cat
last letter of micE
d. = departs, as on timetables

annotation.surface: A cat quickly swallows the last mouse and leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' reads as the adjective, quick; it is a theatre cue, the line a straight man feeds a comic.
annotation.definitionFit: A feed line is a line delivered to prompt a comedian's punchline.
